title: auto-cost-profiles: introduce automated batching/caching defaults and quantization profiles with unit-econ estimator
author: Linnea Park
description:
Motivation: Customers frequently underspec batching and cache config, leading to higher per-token costs. We've also seen ad-hoc quantization usage that causes quality regressions or suboptimal cost savings. This PR adds an automated default picker for batching and KV/prefix cache behavior, a small library of recommended quantization profiles per model family, and a unit-economics estimator in the Console/CLI that projects token-level cost impact for suggested changes.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Adds a new runtime component (cost-optimizer) that suggests safe defaults for request batching, autosize windowing, and prefix/KV cache TTLs based on observed latency distribution and request concurrency.
- Introduces a quant-profiles.yaml catalog with precomputed tradeoffs (FP16/INT8/4-bit tuned variants) and compatibility metadata per model family (hf name patterns).
- Adds a unit-economics estimator endpoint (/internal/v1/cost-estimate) used by Console and the CLI to preview dollar/token savings for a given workload and rollout plan.
- Wire Console UI to surface the top-3 recommended profiles with estimated monthly savings and quality risk score.
- Adds telemetry hooks and a small eval harness to validate quality regressions when a quant profile is applied in canary mode.

Checklist: 
- [x] Runtime: cost-optimizer core and config parsing
- [x] API: cost-estimate endpoint, auth gating
- [x] Console: UI + telemetry preview panel
- [x] CLI: `rw cost preview` command
- [x] Tests: unit tests for profile matching, integration tests for estimator
- [x] Docs: new docs page and quickstart snippets
- [x] Perf: microbenchmarks validating latency impact when defaults are applied

Backward compatibility notes: defaults are opt-in; the runtime will not change existing customer configs unless `enable_auto_cost_profiles=true` is set in cluster config or organization-level setting is toggled via Console. Canary rollouts call the estimator and run eval sets before automatic migration.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: overaggressive batching could increase tail latency for low-concurrency customers. Mitigation: policy enforces latency SLO guardrails and sets per-route max_batch_window defaults conservatively; users can opt-out.
- Risk: quantization can degrade output quality. Mitigation: profiles are annotated with risk_score and recommend canary evaluation sets; automations will not apply profiles if risk_score > 0.6 without explicit consent.

Related work: ENG-1982 (batching improvements), ENG-2041 (KV cache TTLs), INF-73 (quantization tooling), DOCS-421 for console copy.

Testing notes: run `make test-integration` which exercises estimator with 3 synthetic workloads (chat-short, chat-long, embeddings-heavy). Benchmarks included in `benchmark-lab/cost-profiles` show median cost reductions 18-27% for common web-chat shapes using INT8 profiles and prefix caching enabled.

Merge: squash and merge.

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Can we be explicit about the privacy implications of telemetry? We should ensure no PII is sent. — replied: Telemetry is aggregated and token-level payloads are not captured; added doc note and unit test (see tests/telemetry/).

Priya Nair: The default batch window looks aggressive for 99th percentile latency. Suggest lowering to 8ms on first rollout. — replied: lowered conservative default to 8ms and added SLO guardrail check in service.go

Jorge Alvarez: Will quant-profiles.yaml be updated automatically during model onboarding? — replied: added a migration hook in model-registry to annotate new models with candidate profiles; not automatic application.
release_notes: Adds automated cost-optimization tooling: batching and caching defaults, quantization profile catalog, and a unit-economics estimator. Opt-in behind feature flag. See docs/ops/cost-optimization.md for migration steps and Console UX.
